podcast.body: A rock and roll song by Chuck Berry was the sole such track chosen for the Voyager Golden Disk, a phonograph record launched into space with the Voyager I and Voyager II probes in 1977. This means that if an alien civilization ever discovers these probes, their first exposure to rock music will come from Chuck Berry, a Black man. "There is exactly one rock and roll song on the Voyager Golden Disk."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: Chuck Berry's most famous song is cited as demonstrating a very similar structure to Little Richard's, maintaining the same musical canons of the 1950s. It begins with a very acute guitar sound, which then lowers its register when Berry starts singing, and rises again when he pauses, maintaining a continuous high-pitched sonic line. "Este es Chuck Berry cantando Johnny Bigwood que es su canción más famosa."

srcs.episode: Cómo LED ZEPPELIN inventó el ROCK MODERNO

podcast.body: The Beach Boys' song "Fun, Fun, Fun" distinctively opens with an instrumental intro that is directly appropriated from Chuck Berry's iconic "Johnny B. Good." "Fun, fun, fun, have lyrics by Mike Love, saw of his wittiest, and start out with an intro taken straight from Johnny B. Good."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
